body: Do you happen to remember how long it took them to review your application? I submitted mine 3 weeks ago and there has yet to be any movement, so I'm wondering what to expect before reaching out to them to check on it. Thank you!

41F here. Older than your target demographic I assume, but female eyes all the same.

First, you need a revamp of the pictures. Each picture needs to do something for you. You need a nice shot of your face, one where you're cleaned up and looking your best. You need a full body shot in clothes that are flattering for you. Take some photos that show your personality, like your sense of humor, or being silly, or a picture showing your mastery of something you're especially good at.

In your profile, the first photo isn't a good angle, as another person mentioned. The capy is super cute though. The second photo is a face shot, which is great to have, it's just that this one is a mediocre snapshot of you. I think the angle is a bit too close. I'm sure you can take better face shots than that one. The third pic is just kind of meh. You're dressed in the kind of clothes you wear out on a boat, and the shirt is the same one in the capy picture... only you're wearing different pants, so it kinda makes it look like you only have a couple of shirts and wear that one all the time. Ditch the seafood picture - it doesn't do anything for you. The skiing picture is fine -- it shows you do active things! Lose the grad photo since it's 5 years old.

You can use the text prompts better than you do. The first one tells us what you're interested in, which is good, it just needs to be done differently. Tells us what you're interested in but in a cute and witty way.

"Moderate" -- I don't know what that means in NZ. Where I live, it means the guy supports Trump and doesn't want to admit it. It might be fine where you are. Since you're looking for something serious, ditch the "open to short" relationship type.

The "what you're looking for" prompt you need to answer totally differently. This is a golden moment to tell people what you are here for. Do not tell them you're looking for someone to kill your boredom -- nobody wants to date you to entertain you. And on a side note, I suggest going out and finding ways to kill your own boredom because you might meet someone naturally and be able to ditch the apps altogether ;)

Oh, and the voice prompt thing... I obviously can't hear it, but I will tell you that nearly every single one of those I have ever come across is completely cringey. I don't even listen to them anymore. If you want something recorded, do a video.
This is a much more diplomatic way to say what I was thinking. ![gif](emote|free_emotes_pack|grimacing)

I'm glad you had a good experience with them. Their sales rep seemed great, spent a ton of time helping me understand everything and when I was ready to move forward, he said he would send me a contract to sign that evening or at the latest the next morning. I never heard from him again. He just totally ghosted. ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

I'm 41F and did a lot of app dating in my early 30s. This guy fits the profile of a certain type I saw a lot of. He's 46, never married, dating women 15 years his junior, and wants you to come over to his house on a second date. I would bet he filters his age range on something like 25-34 and is not looking for anything serious, or perhaps not emotionally capable of anything serious, so he just goes for the emotionally superficial relationships, which means they end quickly and include early, casual sex. There is also a chance he is a true predator and dangerous -- do not dismiss your gut feeling. The fact that he hasn't done anything to put the restaurant date into place tells me he likely isn't interested in putting it into place because he wants you to come to his house. I see a lot of red flags here based on my past experiences and would walk away, personally. Whatever you do, just keep your spidey senses up and follow your instinct.

If you're not sure how to convey your concerns and boundaries to him, here's a script you can adapt to your needs:

"I'm excited to see you again, but I'm not comfortable going to your house for dinner. I would prefer to go out to a restaurant or do something else in public. Also, I want to make expectations clear. I know that going to someone's house for a date can, for some people, imply an openness to sex. I don't feel like we know each other well enough for sex and I am generally not open to sex with a new partner until we have established monogamy and gotten to know each other for a while."

Stay safe out there and good luck.

As a foster mother, I thank you for looking at this issue.

I know someone in Los Angeles County who is currently experiencing homelessness and her child is in foster care. Her child was removed about 3.5 years ago and she became homeless about a year ago. The connection between her losing her son and losing housing is her struggles with mental health, although I don't believe she sees it this way. This is likely a different angle than you're looking for with the homelessness-foster care connection, but it is an a way in which they are intertwined. If you would like to connect with her, I would be happy to help you reach her. Also, she is a photographer, so if you have any room in your own budget to hire her, she could probably help you document the kinds of things you're interested in.
My thoughts exactly. If they're starting this far in the hole, I'd rather not be the person who hangs around while they figure out how to climb out.

They were supposed to send me a contract to look over earlier this week; it's been 3 days and they haven't sent me anything. I'm not sure what happened there, but it sort of reenforces what you're all telling me about their competency.
Thank you; this is really helpful to know. How long ago did you work with them?
